sessions.feedback: The data was sufficient. Pre-market prints on thin volume (e.g. ESLT +8% on 605 shares, ACM, KNX) are hard to trust, so a pre-market VWAP or a bid/ask indication would help judge the likely opening price. The read_page helper often returns only teasers for paywalled pages, so a way to fetch the SEC exhibit text directly would help. Consensus estimates were not available from the tools and I had to use web search for them.
No blocking issues. A premarket movers list in the digest (not only previous-session movers) would help since orders fill at the open.
No VIX or futures data in tools; would help judge the volatility regime.

summary:
Session 2026-11-17.

Session 2026-11-17 (pre-open). Context: SPY -1.91% and QQQ -2.67% Monday, pre-market flat to +0.3%. NVDA closed 156.14 (+1.2% pre) and reports tonight after the close (consensus about $109B revenue, EPS 2.47); I did not pre-position into the binary event. Warsh speaks today, a Dec Fed hike is priced, 10y about 5.1%. Researched: HD (EPS 3.86 vs 3.84, revenue beat, comp guide narrowed to ~1.4%, CEO change, pre -1.9%: no edge), ACM (+25% run-up before the print, +6% pre: skipped), SMWB and SLS (beat/Phase 3 win, priced), KLAR (+1% pre, Q4 guide AOI $100-120M: no clear edge), JD (slight EPS miss, -4%). Trades: long AS (Amer Sports) 7% on a Q3 beat/raise plus $1B buyback after a 5-day slide, pre +5%; long ESLT (Elbit) 5% on a Q3 beat, record $33B backlog and a 2027 high-teens growth guide, pre +8% on thin volume. Both are 10-day post-earnings drift trades with stops of 8% and 10% and targets of 15%. Check next session: the NVDA reaction at the 11-18 open (entry candidate in NVDA/semis only if a base forms), how AS and ESLT held the gap, retail sales and Waller on 11-18, and the Bessent/Nvidia compliance deadline around 11-26. Other watch names: FTNT, INTC and NOW.
notes:
Session 1 (2026-10-29): Stayed cash. Looked at GOOGL (-12% EPS miss/capex), NOW (-27%), FTNT (-20% despite beat/raise), ADT (take-private, pinned), CROX (+21% priced in).
Session 2 (10-30): Premarket tech selloff: INTC -25%, AMZN -6%, AMD -9%, DELL -8%. Cash.
Session 3 (11-02): SPY -1.77%, QQQ -3.47%, INTC -28.6%, RDDT -29%. Cash.
Session 4 (11-03): Falling knives kept falling: FTNT 126 (-7%), INTC 60 (-8.8%). Lesson: buying rebounds right after a crash would have lost; wait for stabilisation.
Sessions 5-6 (11-10, 11-11): Cash. Hot CPI, 10y near 5%, Fed hike bets. CRWV +24.7% on beat.
Session 7 (11-12): Cash. WSJ: Nvidia board weighed removing Huang. NVDA -8% pre.
Session 8 (11-13): Cash. NVDA closed 166, Huang exit headlines, House subpoena threat.
Session 9 (11-16): Cash. Huang resigned; Bessent demands external CEO, answers in 10 days (~11-26) on China/Singapore chip compliance. TU, CGON, SMMT, PERI all priced/pinned. No trade.
Session 10 (11-17): SPY -1.91%, QQQ -2.67% Monday; pre-market flat/+0.3%. NVDA closed 156.14, reports 11-17 AMC (consensus rev ~$109B, EPS 2.47). Fed Chair Warsh speaks today; Dec hike priced; 10y ~5.1%. First trades: long AS (Amer Sports, Q3 beat/raise/$1B buyback, 5 down days into print, pre +5%) 7% and long ESLT (Elbit, Q3 beat, record backlog $33B, 2027 high-teens growth, 4-day slide, pre +8%) 5%. Both are small-edge post-earnings drift trades from oversold; 10-day horizon, stops 8%/10%. Skipped: HD (beat on EPS 3.86 v 3.84 but pre -1.9%, comps guide narrowed to 1.4%, CEO change), ACM (ran +25% in 20d before print, +6% pre), SMWB/SLS (priced), KLAR (+1%), JD (-4%, EPS slight miss).
Lessons: Catalyst moves in biotech/M&A are priced by open (TU, CGON, SMMT, SLS). Whipsaw tape: gap-ups reversed (CRWV 11-11). Earnings beats where the stock slid into the print and guidance was raised are the best pre-open candidates; fade risk remains (AS fell 10% after Aug 18 beat/raise; FTNT fell 20% on beat/raise 10-29). Review AS/ESLT outcomes vs SPY after 10 days to see if this pattern works.
Open ideas: NVDA/semis after 11-17 earnings reaction (look at 11-18 open; do not pre-position into binary event); FTNT/INTC/NOW once a base forms; Bessent deadline ~11-26; macro 10y ~5%, rate-hike regime hurts long-duration tech. Tomorrow 11-18: retail sales, Waller, Williams; Lowe's/Target/TJX type earnings likely this week.

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is a few high-quality trades.

- Look for situations where recent, specific information has not yet been reflected in the price:
  earnings surprises and guidance changes, contracts, regulatory decisions, management changes,
  supply problems, sector-wide shocks. Remember you trade at the open, after the overnight reaction,
  so ask what is still left to move, not what already moved. It works in both directions: bad
  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.
- Prefer clear catalysts you can verify over vague narratives. A strong case beats a busy portfolio,
  so concentrate on your best ideas. Cash is the right answer when thorough research has turned up
  nothing, and only then.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
- Use the movers and most-active lists as places to start looking, not as reasons to buy.
